commits.subject: Let the user give a reason when removing a message
commits.body:
The protocol carries a reason on a redaction and other clients let the sender
give one, but removing a message here sent the redaction straight away with no
reason and no confirmation.

Removing a message now opens a dialog with an optional reason, and the
redaction is only sent once it is confirmed. A blank reason is sent as none, so
confirming without typing anything behaves exactly as before. A message which
was never sent has nobody to give a reason to, so the send failure dialog's
Remove still redacts it immediately.

commits.subject: Give the removal confirmation the dialog the team asked for
commits.body:
The dialog now reads "Confirm removal" over "Are you sure you wish to remove
this message?", with the reason field marked as optional beneath it, rather
than a bare title and a labelled field. TextFieldDialog gained a supporting
text so the field can carry that note.

The pending removal moves from a nullable timeline item to redactEventAction,
an AsyncAction whose Confirming state carries the event id, so it is modelled
the same way as every other action the user has to confirm.

commits.subject: Ensure we create a fresh Client when the sessionId is know after authentication.
Close the client used to log in before creating the client of the session
commits.body:
Since the login flows stopped handing their client over to
RustMatrixClientFactory and let finalizeClientCreation() build a fresh
one from the SessionData, two problems appeared.

The client built by loginWithQrCode() was never owned by anyone: it is
not assigned to currentClient, so clear() had nothing to close and the
Rust Client stayed open for the whole app lifetime, holding the session
stores of the freshly logged in account. It is now tracked in
currentClient, and also disposed of when the QR login fails, which is
safe because that flow always builds its own client.

The client of the session was also built while the login client was
still open. Both use the same session paths, so their state and crypto
SQLite stores, and the search index when message search is enabled, were
opened twice at the same time with no cross process lock to protect
them. clear() now runs before the final client is created.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Stop deleting the session data of a logged in account on the next login
commits.body:
sessionPaths keeps pointing at the directories of the account which has
just been logged in, and it was never reset. Adding another account
calls setHomeserver(), whose rotateSessionPath() starts by deleting the
directories of the previous sessionPaths, so the file and cache
directories of the first account were wiped.

finalizeClientCreation() now forgets the session paths once the login
succeeded. It is done there rather than in clear() on purpose: after a
failed attempt the directories are orphaned and must still be deleted by
the rotateSessionPath() of the next attempt.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.body:

Add a delayBeforeShowingContent parameter to emptyNode(): when it is finite, a
progress indicator and a "Loading…" label fade in after that delay, reusing the
existing DelayedVisibility helper. It defaults to Duration.INFINITE, so the
splash screen keeps rendering an empty canvas.

Use a one second delay on the two placeholders which are not guaranteed to be

the LoggedInFlowNode one, rendered while the FTUE state is unknown.

commits.subject: Restart the sync service when it stops on an error
commits.body:
Synapse deletes sliding sync connections that have been unused for 7 days. When
an OEM battery manager has kept the application frozen for longer than that, the
next sliding sync request is answered 400 M_UNKNOWN_POS.

The Rust SDK handles that: it resets `pos` and, in offline mode, restarts the
sync. When that recovery gives up, the sync service ends up in the Error or
Terminated state and stops for good, and it is then up to the application to
call start() again. Element X iOS does it, we do not: SyncOrchestrator only
restarts the sync service when its state is Idle, so the sync stays dead for the
rest of the process lifetime.

Nothing recovers from there. The sync never reaches Running, so
waitForE2eeInitializationTasks() never returns, the session verified status
stays Unknown, and the FTUE is stuck on WaitingForInitialState. Clearing the
application data is the only workaround.

Restart the sync service when it is in the Error or Terminated state, with an
exponential backoff from 1s to 30s to avoid hammering a failing homeserver. The
backoff is only reset once the sync service has been running for a while, since
startSync() moves the state to Running right away.

Fixes #7689

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Replace git flow with regular git commands in the release script V2
commits.body:
The script was relying on the external git-flow tool and on a local
`git config gitflow.*` initialisation, which made its behaviour depend on
the machine setup and hid what was actually done to the branches.

The release branch is now created with `git checkout -b`, and the release
is finished with explicit merge, tag, back-merge and branch deletion
commands. The merge and tag messages are provided explicitly so that the
generated history stays identical to the previous releases. Each step now
aborts the script with a clear message when it fails, instead of letting
the script continue.

Note that tools/release/release.sh (V1) still uses git flow.

commits.subject: Replace String by AccountProvider to be able to get baseUrl and serverName.
Close the threaded timeline created by PollRepository
commits.body:
PollRepository created a dedicated timeline for each operation performed in a
thread, and never closed it, leaking SDK resources. Replace getTimelineProvider()
with a scoped withTimeline() helper, so that the created timeline is closed once
the operation completes, whether it succeeds, fails or gets cancelled.

The live timeline is left untouched, since it is owned by its room.

commits.body:
The problem seemed to be sometimes the background work to switch from live timeline to a focused event timeline wasn't finished in time and an assertion failed from time to time.

By providing the coroutine to run this on we can pass a `TestScope` and force it to reliably run immediately instead in unit tests.

commits.subject: Close the threaded timelines created by ShareLocationPresenter and DefaultMediaSender
commits.body:
Both created a dedicated timeline for each operation performed in a thread, and
never closed it, leaking SDK resources. Apply the same treatment as PollRepository:
replace getTimeline() with a scoped withTimeline() helper, which closes the created
timeline once the operation completes, whether it succeeds, fails or gets cancelled.

In DefaultMediaSender.sendGallery(), waiting for the upload handler is now done
inside the block, so that the timeline stays open until the upload completes.

commits.subject: Use patched Konsist version (forked, 0.18.0) (#7719)
commits.body:
* Use a patched fork of Konsist

The patch contains code to ignore hidden folders in the root project: by default, Konsist scans *every single file* in the root directory except for a few exceptions, and hidden folders were not a part of that.

That means `.git`, `.github`, etc. would be scanned to for no good reason and even worse,  hidden folders used for worktrees would get scanned too, so Konsist would end up scanning the same project with small variations several times and OOMing / taking ages to finish.

* Make `Immutable/Stable` annotation check more performant. Also, fix case that was previously not found
